deck.audience: Engineering leaders, CTOs, and developer experience teams evaluating technology strategy and hiring priorities

brief.title: State of Developer Ecosystem 2024: Language Trends, Satisfaction, and Strategic Shifts
brief.one_liner: Key insights from JetBrains' survey of 23,262 developers on programming language usage, satisfaction, adoption intent, and domain specialization trends from 2017 to 2024.
brief.goal: Help engineering leaders understand which languages are growing or declining, where developer satisfaction is highest, and how language choice maps to application domains — enabling better technology strategy and hiring decisions.

slides.title: State of Developer Ecosystem 2024: Language Trends, Satisfaction, and Strategic Shifts
slides.objective: Cover slide introducing the report: JetBrains' annual survey of 23,262 developers worldwide. Set context that this is the most comprehensive snapshot of the developer community, covering languages, tools, AI attitudes, and career trends.

slides.title: Python Closes the Gap: 8 Years of Language Usage Shifts
slides.objective: Present the multi-year language usage trend data (2017-2024) in a line chart or table. Highlight JavaScript peaking at 70% in 2020 before declining to 61% (from 65% in 2017), Python rising from 32% to 57%, TypeScript tripling from 12% to 37%, and PHP dropping from 30% to 17%. Show that the top-5 landscape is reshuffling.

slides.title: Python Is Now the #1 Primary Language at 35%
slides.objective: Show the primary language breakdown with a horizontal bar chart: Python 35%, Java 30%, JavaScript 28%, TypeScript 19%, SQL 17%. Contrast primary usage with adoption intent (all below 6%) to illustrate ecosystem lock-in and the comfort zone effect.

slides.title: TypeScript and Rust Top Developer Satisfaction, Nearly Tied at 199 vs 198
slides.objective: Display the language satisfaction ranking as a bar chart: TypeScript 199, Rust 198, Python 151, Go 129, Lua 118, C++ 113, Kotlin 113, Shell 100, Dart 93, C 86. Highlight that type-safe, modern-tooling languages dominate the top spots.

slides.title: Each Language Owns a Domain: AI Belongs to Python, UI to TypeScript
slides.objective: Present the language-by-domain heatmap or a summary table showing which language dominates each application area. Python leads AI/ML (31%) and data science (28%); TypeScript/JavaScript own UI (62%/58%); Java leads APIs & services (49%); C++ leads system tools & components (27%). Show that language choice is driven by domain, not general preference.

slides.title: What This Means for Your Technology Strategy in 2025
slides.objective: Summarize actionable insights: (1) Invest in Python for AI/ML teams — it is the undisputed leader; (2) TypeScript is the future of frontend and full-stack; (3) Rust and Go are the growth plays for infrastructure and systems; (4) PHP and Ruby hiring pools are shrinking; (5) Developer satisfaction correlates with type safety and modern tooling — factor this into retention strategy.
